author: IOL
title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to reach League Cup quarter-finals
text: Everton dispatch Newcastle to reach League Cup quarter-finals Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach the League Cup quarter-finals against minnows Fleetwood. Everton' boss David Moyes was delighted with the way side dismantled Newcastle to advance in the EFL Cup. Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood. David Moyes's side took the lead through James Garner's first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn's reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run. Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14.The 'Cod Army' caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury. Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph.British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes's men made light work of their last-16 tie. Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James' Park on Monday. Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection\"due to a breach of club discipline\".Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training. Everton hit their stride Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock's low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar's long-range strike moments later. Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January.At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek. Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval. Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock's pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford.Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season. Burn scored with a header from Willock's 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players. But Newcastle's brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Everton moved a step closer to Wembley.
